questions.q: What makes a guest user fundamentally different from every other user type covered in this course?
options: Every anonymous visitor to a site shares one single profile simultaneously, with no individual login or session to audit
Guest users have more permissions than System Administrators by default
Guest users must log in with a shared password
Guest users only exist in Developer Edition orgs
questions.explain: A guest user isn't one person — it's the shared identity every unauthenticated visitor operates as at the same time, which is why guest misconfigurations are categorically riskier.

questions.q: What does 'Secure guest user record access' require, and can it be turned off?
options: It is optional and can be disabled by any System Administrator
It only applies to custom objects, never standard ones
It requires explicit grants (sharing rules or sharing sets) for guest record access, and it cannot be disabled
It automatically deletes guest user sessions after 10 minutes
questions.explain: Since Summer '20 this is a mandatory platform-level setting — guest users can no longer get implicit access from a permissive OWD, and the setting can't be turned off.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend granting Create (not Read) on Lead for a public lead-capture form guest profile?
options: Because Read is always required regardless of the form's purpose
Because Create and Read are the same permission in guest profiles
Because Lead records cannot be created by guest users under any configuration
Because the form's actual function only needs Create, and granting Read just because it's convenient to test with adds unnecessary exposure
questions.explain: The lesson's principle is granting only what the site's actual functionality needs — a submission form needs Create, not Read access to existing leads.

questions.q: Why are sharing sets recommended over broad sharing rules for guest user record access?
options: Sharing sets are faster to configure but functionally identical
Sharing sets scope access to records related to the visitor's own session context, which is narrower than a sharing rule applied broadly to the whole guest profile
Sharing rules cannot be used with guest users at all
Sharing sets grant access to every record in the org automatically
questions.explain: A sharing set narrows access to what's relevant to that visitor's own interaction (like a case they just submitted), rather than opening broader access to the entire guest profile.

questions.q: What is the common root cause behind real, publicized guest-user data exposures, according to this lesson?
options: A guest profile accumulating more access than the site needs — often granted during testing and never narrowed before launch
A Salesforce platform bug unrelated to configuration
Guest users guessing employee passwords
Sharing sets being too restrictive
questions.explain: The lesson describes a consistent pattern: broad access granted for convenience during development, left in place at launch, and reachable by anyone on the internet with no login required.
